facts.statement: The genus Paramylostoma was described by Dunkle and Bungart in 1945.
Paramylostoma lived during the Late Famennian stage.
Paramylostoma is classified as a genus.
The species Paramylostoma arcualis is the only known species in the genus.
Paramylostoma belongs to the family Selenosteidae.
Paramylostoma is a member of the class Placodermi.
Paramylostoma lived between 365.2 and 358.86 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Famennian to Famennian (365.2 to 358.86 million years ago)

facts.statement: Fossils of Paramylostoma arcualis have been found in the Cleveland Shale of Ohio.
facts.quote: from the Late Famennian Cleveland Shale of Late Devonian Ohio

facts.statement: Paramylostoma arcualis had a compressed, box-like head, thoracic armor, and large, rounded orbits.
facts.quote: It has a compressed, box-like head and thoracic armor, and large, rounded orbits.

facts.statement: Compared to other selenosteids like Selenosteus, Paramylostoma arcualis had relatively small orbits.
facts.quote: However, in comparison with other selenosteids, such as Selenosteus, P. arcualis orbits were rather small.

facts.statement: Paramylostoma arcualis likely had a durophagous diet, indicated by its smooth jaws.
facts.quote: P. arcualis had smooth jaws that suggest the animal was durophagous.
